title: Redwood Discovery: Model selection - Empirical AI
meeting_header: Attendees: Jenna Marshall (Redwood AE), Miguel Ortega (Redwood SE), Dana Li (Empirical AI - CTO), Ravi Singh (Empirical AI - ML Eng), Marta Gomez (Empirical AI - Platform)
summary: Initial model-selection discovery for Empirical AI evaluating Redwood Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. Key constraints: 64k+ context for long-docs, multilingual support (EN/ES/FR), tool/function calling for knowledge-base lookups, latency targets for realtime features, and security (SOC2, SSO, VPC/KMS). Discussed open model tradeoffs, quantization/throughput, and pilot/benchmark next steps.
topics: Current infra & existing inference (SageMaker and on-prem kubernetes)
Tool calling / function-calling support and routing
action_items: Jenna Marshall: Share hosted pricing sheet + Dedicated sizing template (due: 2026-03-20)
Miguel Ortega: Run quick perf estimate for Mixtral-8x7B vs Mistral-instruct on our 64k token profile (due: 2026-03-22)
Ravi Singh: Provide sample dataset & typical prompt patterns (due: 2026-03-19)
Marta Gomez: Confirm compliance checklist items required for Private deployment (due: 2026-03-24)
next_steps: Redwood to provision 48h pilot for hosted 64k config and share benchmark template
Customer to send sample prompts and a small doc corpus for quality/perf eval
Schedule SE-led technical deep-dive next week to discuss VPC networking and KMS integration
transcript: [00:00] Jenna Marshall: Hi everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Jenna from Redwood, AE on this account. Miguel from our SE team is with me. Dana, thanks for making time.
[00:12] Dana Li: Yep, thanks. We wanted to get into model selection — especially open models. We're evaluating early for a pilot, trying to understand hosted vs dedicated vs private options.

[00:26] Miguel Ortega: Great. Quick intro from our side: we help run inference across hosted, dedicated reserve pools, and private VPC/on-prem. Today we want to understand your requirements so we can recommend model families and deployment modality.

[00:40] Ravi Singh: Our main product is a long-form analysis assistant — customers upload long reports, we summarize, answer follow-ups. So context length is the first big constraint: some docs are 200k characters, so we're looking at 64k token context ideally.
[01:05] Jenna Marshall: Got it. When you say 64k tokens, is that a hard requirement for the pilot, or can you accept chunking/augmentation with retrieval?

[01:15] Ravi Singh: For some workflows chunking is fine, but for the real-time assisted editing feature we want seamless context — so higher native context is better to reduce hallucination from retrieval boundaries.
[01:34] Marta Gomez: Also multilingual: EN/ES/FR, maybe Portuguese later. Model should be decent across those languages — particularly Spanish customer support docs.

[01:47] Miguel Ortega: Noted. There are tradeoffs: the larger context models and 64k variants often come with higher compute. We can explore quantized variants and caching to help unit cost. For model families, are you leaning open-source only?

[02:05] Dana Li: Prefer open models for licensing and control. We're benchmarking Mistral, Llama family, and Mixtral (heard good things about Mixtral's multilingual), and a few instruction-tuned forks.

[02:20] Jenna Marshall: Cool. Two immediate practical questions: tool/function calling support — do you need function calling like structured API calls from the model? And latency SLOs — what's acceptable for interactive flows?

[02:35] Ravi Singh: Yes function calling is critical — we call backend KB lookup APIs and internal tools. Latency target is sub-second for token generation in the editor path; end-to-end maybe 400-800ms for short responses.

[02:53] Miguel Ortega: Okay latency and function-calling are feasible but depend on model choice and batching. For sub-second we often recommend smaller quantized models on Dedicated if you need high concurrency; Hosted can do it too but needs the right instance profile.
[03:10] Dana Li: On security: we must be SOC 2 compliant, and for some customers data can't leave our VPC. So Private deployment or Redwood Dedicated with VPC peering would be options.

[03:24] Jenna Marshall: We support Private with customer-managed control plane + KMS/HSM integrations, and Dedicated can be provisioned in a VPC with private links. We'll follow up with the compliance pack.
[03:36] Marta Gomez: For Private, we need to know upgrade cadence and who manages kernel/accel drivers — it's a big ops asks for us.

[03:46] Miguel Ortega: Understood. For Private we provide an on-prem package; customer ops manage base infra but Redwood provides the runtime and upgrade artifacts. We'll include an ops runbook in the next packet.
[04:02] Jenna Marshall: Returning to models: Miguel, can you give a quick sketch of tradeoffs between Mistral family, Llama-based weights, and Mixtral-style models for our usecases?

[04:15] Miguel Ortega: Sure. High level: Llama derivatives (Llama 2 and some forks) have large community and fine-tuning support — good for instruction-following; they have 32k and some 64k context variants. Mistral tends to be strong on single-shot instruction and has efficient inference; Mixtral and some multilingual-specialized models often have stronger Spanish/French out of the box. But performance depends on tokenization and instruction tuning; you'll want to run quality tests on your support docs.
[04:47] Dana Li: Any concerns about hallucinations with these open models, especially on domain-specific legal/medical-similar text?

[04:56] Miguel Ortega: Hallucinations remain a model-level issue. Mitigation: retrieval-augmented prompting, strong prompt engineering, and temperature/penalty tuning. Also tool-calling with ground-truth KB lookups reduces hallucination risk. Redwood's routing can fallback to smaller deterministic models for factual tasks if desired.
[05:18] Ravi Singh: You mentioned routing — could Redwood route by latency vs cost? For example route premium users to low-latency Dedicated nodes and others to cheaper hosted quantized variants?

[05:29] Miguel Ortega: Exactly. Smart routing is something we provide — by policy you can send requests to different model variants, regions, or capacity tiers. It also supports automatic fallback if a model variant is out of capacity.
[05:44] Jenna Marshall: Quick aside: transcription note — Miguel said "K-V cash" earlier, that's KV cache. Apologies, auto-transcription is messy sometimes.

[05:51] Dana Li: No worries, that's normal. On the pilot: ideally we run hosted pilot first to validate quality then evaluate Dedicated for latency/cost and Private for compliance. Is that the usual flow?

[06:05] Jenna Marshall: Yes, many customers do a hosted pilot and then move to Dedicated or Private depending on security and cost. Vendor lock-in risk is low — you can pin model versions and rollouts.
[06:18] Ravi Singh: For the hosted pilot, will you support our 64k workload? We've heard some hosted vendors only support 32k on shared infra.

[06:28] Miguel Ortega: We have hosted options that support 64k for select models; capacity is limited compared to 32k but we can provision a short pilot environment. If you need consistent throughputs, Dedicated is the better long-term option.
[06:42] Marta Gomez: Cost is also a consideration. What's the rough cost difference between hosted 64k vs Dedicated quantized replicas?

[06:50] Miguel Ortega: Ballpark: hosted 64k on large GPU instances will be higher per-token than a Dedicated quantized fleet optimized for your workload. That said, Dedicated has commit/seat economics — a lot depends on throughput and concurrency.
[07:05] Dana Li: On function calling — how robust is Redwood's support? We need typed schema return and orchestration for multi-step tool chains.

[07:15] Miguel Ortega: We support function/tool calling semantics and structured outputs. There can be some differences across model families on how reliably they follow schemas; we recommend a small test harness with your tool definitions to surface issues quickly.
[07:30] Ravi Singh: For multilingual accuracy, can you run a quick eval on our Spanish corpus? We'll share a 500-document sample.
[07:37] Jenna Marshall: Yes please send the sample. Miguel will run a comparative eval across your shortlisted models and return a report.
[07:45] Miguel Ortega: I will. I'll likely test Mixtral-style multilingual variant, Mistral-instruct, and a Llama-64k tuned variant, and include latency and token cost estimates.
[07:58] Dana Li: What about quantization? We need to preserve some accuracy but reduce footprint. Any recommendations?

[08:06] Miguel Ortega: 4-bit quantization works well for many instruction tasks, but you may see small regression on subtle reasoning. We can run ablations; Redwood Optimize can recommend the quant profiles per workload.
[08:20] Marta Gomez: Networking: for Dedicated in our AWS account, does Redwood require peering or private link? How does SSO integrate?
[08:30] Miguel Ortega: We support VPC peering, PrivateLink, and dedicated endpoints. For SSO we integrate with SAML/SSO and RBAC. We'll include a network diagram in the follow-up packet.

[08:43] Jenna Marshall: Let's capture the immediate asks: you'll send sample corpus and prompt patterns; we'll run a hosted 48h pilot with 64k config and run model comparisons; we'll share pricing and Dedicated sizing.
[08:56] Dana Li: Sounds good. One more: audit logs and retention for Private — we need 7 years for specific records for compliance. Is that supported?
[09:07] Miguel Ortega: We provide audit logs; retention policies can be configured for Dedicated/Private. We'll confirm the exact retention guarantees and whether we can export to your logging stack.
[09:18] Ravi Singh: Ok. For the pilot, do you need a service account or API key from us?
[09:24] Jenna Marshall: We'll provision Redwood side. For import of docs into the test corpus, a secure upload method is best — we'll share an S3 presign or secure transfer.
[09:33] Dana Li: Fine. Any blockers on our side? We're mostly internal approvals and legal review for hosting agreements.
[09:40] Jenna Marshall: We'll include a copy of our security pack and enterprise terms to start legal review.
[09:48] Miguel Ortega: I'll note to include specifics on KMS/HSM integrations for Private and the responsibilities matrix for on-prem upgrades.
[09:57] Dana Li: Timeline question: we want a pilot in the next two weeks if possible.
[10:02] Jenna Marshall: We can do hosted pilot within 48-72 hours of receiving the sample corpus and signed pilot NDA. We'll aim to kick off by 2026-03-20.
[10:12] Marta Gomez: Good. Let's plan a deeper technical call after the initial results to talk about Dedicated sizing.
[10:18] Jenna Marshall: Agreed — Miguel will lead that session. Any other open questions?
[10:24] Ravi Singh: Not from me. Just to reiterate: tool-calling reliability and 64k context quality are our top two evaluation axes.
[10:33] Jenna Marshall: Understood. We'll prioritize those in the benchmark. Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the artifact pack and scheduling links.
[10:42] Dana Li: Thanks Jenna, Miguel. Looking forward to the results.
[10:46] Jenna Marshall: Bye all.
[10:48] END OF TRANSCRIPT
